Axiom:
Discovering mid-flight that the spec / ticket is silent on a decision the work needs is NOT a reason to interrupt the operator. Decide it yourself — in the spirit of the artifact and `AX_RELEASE_READY_DEFAULT` — then append a ticket-local Decision Log entry (`-D-N · ` → why ↳ rejected, ADR-compact, direct `Edit` — `AX_TICKET_WRITE_SCOPE` treats this section as writable for exactly this purpose) at the point of decision, not after the fact; then continue. A worker additionally tags its `**Handoff →**` line with `deviations: [: , ...]` (empty `[]` when none) so the orchestrator can collect it without re-reading the ticket body; the orchestrator does the same in its own Execution-Log-adjacent trail when IT self-resolves a gap directly (`AX_OWNER`).
Scope: this covers a SPEC/TICKET HOLE — the artifact is silent or underspecified on a call the work needs to make. It does NOT cover an environment/infra blocker (`AX_BLOCKER_ESCALATION`, `H_PAUSED_AWAITING_OPERATOR`) or a risk-acceptance on an open `MAJOR` audit finding (execute STEP_6_BRANCH) — both stay a pause; they are about risk and environment, not a gap in the spec. Test: "can I honor the artifact's stated intent with a sound default?" → self-resolve; "does proceeding need the operator's own risk tolerance, or an environment I cannot fix?" → pause.
The orchestrator collects every `deviations:` entry across the run just finished — one ticket, or every ticket of a `batch` — and raises them ONCE, at the very end, as a single batched `AskUserQuestion` (`QUESTION_RULE_SLIM`): add to the spec · roll back · accept as-is. Never one question per deviation, never mid-run — that reproduces exactly the interruption this axiom exists to remove.
